Konjunktiv I in Reported Speech: B2 Practice

Study four German examples with English meanings, then try four questions and check the explained answers.

B2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the rule

Formal reported speech often marks a statement as reported rather than confirmed: Er sagt, er sei krank. Common forms include sei, habe, könne and werde. If a Konjunktiv I form looks identical to Indikativ, writers often use Konjunktiv II or another reporting construction.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not present reported claims as verified facts. Er sagt, er sei ... signals attribution.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Er sagt, er sei müde.He says that he is tired.
Worked example 2Sie erklärt, sie habe keine Zeit.She explains that she has no time.
Worked example 3Der Sprecher sagt, man könne später beginnen.The speaker says it is possible to start later.
Worked example 4Sie behauptet, er werde bald kommen.She claims that he will come soon.

Practice: fill in the gaps

Put the verb in brackets into Konjunktiv I for reported speech. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Er sagt, er ___ krank. (sein, K I)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: sei

Konjunktiv I third-person singular of sein.

Question 2. Sie sagt, sie ___ Hunger. (haben, K I)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: habe

Konjunktiv I third-person singular of haben.

Question 3. Er erklärt, man ___ die Tür öffnen. (können, K I)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: könne

Konjunktiv I third-person singular of können.

Question 4. Sie sagt, der Bus ___ später fahren. (werden, K I)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: werde

Konjunktiv I third-person singular of werden.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
